Subject: Acme - Post-call TCO recap & recommended next steps

Tom / Sara —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the levers we discussed to help hit your cost targets. I summarized pain, goals, and a few suggested next steps so we have alignment: 

Pain / constraints we heard
- Token cost is the single largest line item for your ML infra; current spend variability makes forecasting hard.
- Tight budget for Q2: you mentioned a hard cap of ~$30k/month for inference.
- Live latency requirement for chat (95th <= 350ms) and occasional batch jobs for nightly analytics.

Goals
- Reduce per-session inference cost by ~35-45% versus current provider while keeping quality parity.
- Keep 95th latency under 350ms for user-facing paths.
- Pilot on 2 high-volume intents in April, then expand if cost/quality checks pass.

Recommended cost/TCO levers (high level)
1) Model & quantization profile: pick an FP16 or 8-bit quantized variant that preserves top-line quality for your prompts (we can A/B). Estimated 20–30% token cost reduction.
2) Batching & concurrency: route background analytics to larger batch sizes; keep user-facing routes on small batches. Could save 10–25% on per-token GPU overhead.
3) KV prefix caching for chat: for repeat system prompts & session prefixes we expect 15–30% token reduction on active users.
4) Dynamic model routing: use a cheaper model for low-risk intents (FAQ) and high-quality model for creative/critical paths. ~10–40% savings depending on traffic mix.

Rough token economics (illustrative)
- Your ballpark: ~120M tokens/month across prod intents today.
- Current blended cost (provider X): $0.50 / 1k tokens -> ~$60k/month.
- Target (with levers above): blended $0.25–0.35 / 1k tokens -> ~$30–42k/month.
- Quick ROI framing: expected 30–50% reduction in month-1 run rate, payback on integration within the quarter given traffic and expected margin improvements.

Attachments: I attached the TCO workbook (acme-tco-workbook.xlsx) and a short pricing summary (redwood-pricing-summary.pdf). The workbook includes a scenario tab where I modeled batch size, cache hit rate, and quantization impact — happy to walk through line by line.

Proposed next steps
- Mar 8–10: 60-minute technical pilot planning call (involve infra + SRE) to agree on metrics and access.
- Mar 15: provide access to a pilot environment (we’ll share a small API key scoped to test data).
- Deliverable by Mar 30: pilot TCO report + latency/quality metrics for the 2 intents.

Would you be open to the planning call next week? If Mar 9 looks okay I’ll send a calendar invite and the pilot checklist.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
